lessons.title: Course Setup
lessons.summary: How the course works, the five tracks, and the free accounts you need
goals: Pick the track that matches your role
Set up free OpenAI and Anthropic developer accounts
Know where each provider publishes its official material
lessons.why: OpenAI and Anthropic each publish courses, docs, cookbooks and research, but the material is spread across a dozen sites. This course puts it in one order so you can learn step by step. Every link points to an official source, so you can trust what you read and cite it at work.
openai: API, Agents SDK, Codex and Apps SDK docs
anthropic: 22 free courses for workers, builders and leaders
Every model capability and tool in one table
Notebooks for tool use, RAG, agents and more
try: Open the interactive learning path and choose a track.
Create a developer account with each provider and generate one API key.
Bookmark both academies; you will return to them in several lessons.
check: Which of the five tracks fits your role today, and which one would you take next?
Where would you look first for a runnable code example from each provider?
Why does it matter that every resource in this course comes from an official source?

lessons.title: AI Foundations
lessons.summary: How language models work, what they do well, and where they fail
goals: Explain in plain words how a language model produces an answer
Name the common failure modes: made-up facts, stale knowledge, missing context
Review AI output with a simple checklist before you use it
lessons.why: Every later lesson assumes you know what a model can and cannot do. Leaders need this to set realistic expectations, and builders need it to design checks around weak spots. Both academies start here for good reason.
openai: AI basics, prompting, context, reviewing outputs · 60–75 min
Turn prompts into repeatable workflows · 75–90 min
anthropic: Work with AI effectively, efficiently, ethically and safely
A plain introduction to how AI works
try: Pick a task you do every week, such as a status summary.
Ask a model to do it twice: once with no context, once with your notes pasted in.
Mark every claim in both answers as correct, wrong or unverifiable, and note what the context changed.
check: Why can a model state something false with full confidence?
What is the difference between a model's training knowledge and the context you give it?
What three checks would you run before sending AI-written work to your manager?

lessons.title: Prompting and Context
lessons.summary: Write instructions models follow reliably, and give them the right context
goals: Structure a prompt with role, task, context, format and examples
Explain why context matters more than clever wording
Turn a one-off prompt into a reusable template
lessons.why: Most poor AI output comes from vague instructions or missing context. Learning to brief a model well is the cheapest quality gain available. The same skill carries over directly to agents, where the brief becomes a system prompt.
openai: AI Foundations: prompting and context modules
Instructions, roles and prompt structure in the API
anthropic: Official techniques for clear, reliable prompts
Effective context engineering for AI agents
Why context is the scarce resource
try: Take the weekly task from Lesson 1 and write a prompt with five labeled parts: role, task, context, output format, one example.
Run it three times and compare the outputs for consistency.
Save the version that works as a template with placeholders.
check: Which part of a prompt most often fixes inconsistent output?
When should you add an example instead of more instructions?
How does a reusable template reduce review effort for a team?

lessons.title: AI Assistants and Agents at Work
lessons.summary: Use ChatGPT and Claude for real work with your own files, and hand off multi-step tasks you can check
goals: Use an AI assistant for research, writing and analysis with your own files
Hand a multi-step task to an agent feature and review what it did
Build a weekly routine around the tasks AI does well for you
lessons.why: Most people meet AI through ChatGPT or Claude, not through code. The real value comes from moving past one-off questions to repeatable tasks with your own files and a clear review step. Both academies built their most popular courses around this kind of everyday work.
openai: Turn tasks into repeatable workflows with review points · 75–90 min
Delegate structured tasks with checkpoints and oversight · 75–90 min
The Apply AI at Work pathway and more
anthropic: Claude for everyday work and its core features
Hand Claude multi-step work on real files and projects
Versions for small businesses, nonprofits, educators and creative work
try: Pick three tasks you do every week, such as a summary, a draft and a small analysis.
Do each one with an AI assistant using your own files, then do the longest one with an agent feature such as ChatGPT's agent mode or Claude Cowork.
Note the time each took and every correction you made, and keep the version that saved the most time for next week.
check: Which task gave the best result, and what made it different from the others?
What did you have to correct, and what does that tell you about where review is needed?
Which of your tasks would you never hand off fully, and why?
lessons.compare: The skills are the same on both sides, so start with the assistant your organization already licenses. OpenAI Academy teaches this as repeatable workflows with review points. Anthropic's courses start from Claude's own features and add versions for specific sectors, which helps if you work in a small business, a nonprofit or education.

lessons.title: What Makes an Agent
lessons.summary: Workflows versus agents, and when an agent is worth building
goals: Tell a fixed workflow apart from an agent
Name the three parts of every agent: model, tools, instructions
Decide whether a use case needs an agent at all
lessons.why: Many teams build agents for jobs a simple workflow would do better. Both providers' foundational guides argue for starting simple and adding autonomy only when it earns its keep. This lesson gives you the vocabulary to make that call.
openai: A practical guide to building agents
When to build, core parts, orchestration, guardrails
Delegate tasks to agents with oversight · 75–90 min
anthropic: Workflows versus agents, and the common building blocks
Why general agents plus skills beat many specialized agents
try: List five tasks your team wants to automate.
For each, decide: single prompt, fixed workflow, or agent, and write one sentence on why.
Pick the one that truly needs an agent and sketch its model, tools and instructions.
check: What is the main risk of choosing an agent when a workflow would do?
What signals tell you a task needs open-ended decision making?
How would you explain the difference to a non-technical executive?

lessons.title: Working with the Model APIs
lessons.summary: Call models from code with the Responses API and the Messages API
goals: Send a first request with each provider's SDK
Explain messages, roles, tokens and streaming
Choose between the two providers' core APIs for a simple app
lessons.why: Every product, agent and integration in this course sits on top of these two APIs. Once you can call them directly, the SDKs and frameworks in later lessons stop feeling like magic. This is also where cost and latency first become visible.
openai: The core API for text, tools and multi-turn state
Five sessions from API foundations to production
anthropic: The core API the SDKs build on
try: Install the official Python SDK for each provider.
Send the same prompt template from Lesson 2 to both APIs and print the responses.
Log token usage for each call and estimate what 1,000 calls a day would cost.
check: What is a token, and why does it drive both cost and speed?
What does streaming change for the person using your app?
Where in each API do you put standing instructions versus the user's message?

lessons.title: Tool Use and Function Calling
lessons.summary: Let models call your code, search the web and act on real systems
goals: Define a tool with a clear name, description and input schema
Run the request → tool call → result → answer loop
Write tool descriptions a model can use correctly
lessons.why: Tools are what turn a model from a writer into a worker. Nearly every agent failure traces back to a confusing tool or a missing one. Learning to design tools well pays off in every later lesson.
openai: Let models call your own code
Built-in web search, file search, code interpreter, MCP
anthropic: Every built-in tool and how it is supported
try: Write one tool, get_order_status(order_id), backed by a small dictionary of fake orders.
Connect it to each provider and ask 'Where is order 1042?'
Rewrite the tool description twice and note when the model calls it correctly.
check: Who actually runs the tool: the model or your code?
What makes a tool description easy for a model to use correctly?
When would you use a built-in tool instead of writing your own?

lessons.title: Structured Outputs
lessons.summary: Generate schema-constrained JSON and handle validation failures
goals: Define a JSON schema for a model's answer
Turn free text into records your systems can store
Handle refusals and missing fields safely
lessons.why: Business systems need fields, not paragraphs. Structured outputs let AI feed spreadsheets, CRMs and dashboards without fragile parsing. This is often the first AI feature that reaches production inside a company.
openai: Guarantee JSON that matches your schema
anthropic: JSON outputs and strict tool use
try: Collect five customer emails, real or invented.
Define a schema with fields for intent, urgency, product and next step.
Extract all five with each provider and load the results into a spreadsheet.
check: What is the difference between asking for JSON and enforcing a schema?
How should your code respond when a required field is missing?
Which of your current reports could be filled by structured outputs?

lessons.title: Retrieval and Agentic RAG
lessons.summary: Ground answers in your own documents and data
goals: Explain the retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) flow
Use a built-in file search tool and compare it with your own pipeline
Measure whether retrieved answers are actually correct
lessons.why: Most company questions depend on company documents a model has never seen. Retrieval lets the model answer from your sources and cite them. Agentic RAG goes further and lets the model decide what to search for next.
openai: Retrieval pipelines and answer-quality checks · 100 min
anthropic: A method that improves retrieval accuracy
try: Upload three policy or product documents to a file search tool.
Write ten questions with known answers and run them.
Score each answer as correct, partly correct or wrong, and note whether it cited the right source.
check: Why does chunking strategy affect answer quality?
What makes retrieval 'agentic' rather than a single search?
How would you prove to a stakeholder that your RAG answers are reliable?
lessons.compare: OpenAI's file search gives you hosted retrieval over your files, which is the quicker way to a first working version. Anthropic's material teaches a retrieval method you assemble yourself, which takes more work and gives you more control over how documents are split and found. Begin with the hosted option, then move to your own pipeline if answer quality on your documents falls short.

lessons.title: Multimodal: Vision, Audio and Voice
lessons.summary: Work with images, speech and real-time voice
goals: Send images to a model and extract information from them
Choose between speech-to-text, text-to-speech and real-time voice
Design a voice interaction that handles interruptions
lessons.why: A large share of business information lives in screenshots, scanned forms, charts and calls. Multimodal models can read and respond to all of it. Voice also opens AI to people who will never type a prompt.
anthropic: Image and PDF support across the platform
try: Take a screenshot of a chart from a real report.
Ask each model to extract the data as a table and summarize the trend.
Check every number against the original and note any errors.
check: What kinds of images still cause extraction mistakes?
When is a chained speech pipeline better than a real-time voice model?
Which workflow in your team starts with a document or a phone call?

lessons.title: Agent Frameworks: OpenAI Agents SDK and Claude Agent SDK
lessons.summary: Build your first agent with each provider's official SDK
goals: Run each provider's agent quickstart
Add a tool and a guardrail to an agent
Read traces to see what the agent actually did
lessons.why: The SDKs handle the loop, tool execution and state so you can focus on the job. Each one reflects how its provider thinks agents should be built. Running both side by side is the fastest way to learn what is common and what is a design choice.
anthropic: The Claude Code agent loop as a library
Build a bug-fixing agent in minutes
Building agents with the Claude Agent SDK
Example agents to run and read
try: Complete both quickstarts.
Give each agent the get_order_status tool from Lesson 6.
Ask a question that needs two tool calls and compare the traces.
check: What does the SDK do for you that you did by hand in Lesson 6?
Where would you add a guardrail in each SDK?
What did the traces reveal that the final answer hid?
lessons.compare: The OpenAI Agents SDK gives you separate parts for agents, tools, handoffs, guardrails and tracing, which suits workflows where several agents pass work to each other. The Claude Agent SDK packages the agent loop behind Claude Code as a library, which suits agents that read files and run commands. Choose by the kind of work your agent does, then run the quickstart for that SDK first.

lessons.title: Multi-Agent Systems and Orchestration
lessons.summary: Handoffs, subagents and when splitting work across agents helps
goals: Compare handoffs, manager agents and subagents
Explain when parallel agents speed things up and when they waste tokens
Design a two-agent system with a clear division of work
lessons.why: Splitting work across agents can improve quality and speed, and it can also multiply cost and confusion. Anthropic's research system and OpenAI's orchestration recipes show both sides. The goal is to know which problems actually benefit.
openai: Deep Research API with the Agents SDK
anthropic: How we built our multi-agent research system
Use subagents to manage context and delegate
try: Design a research assistant with one lead agent and two specialist agents.
Write the brief the lead agent sends to each specialist.
Run it on one question and compare the cost and quality with a single agent.
check: What kinds of tasks gain the most from parallel agents?
Why does a clear brief between agents matter so much?
How would you decide a multi-agent design is not worth its cost?

lessons.title: Memory and Context Engineering
lessons.summary: Keep agents on track across long tasks and many sessions
goals: Explain why context windows fill up and what happens when they do
Use compaction, memory files and conversation state
Decide what an agent should remember and what it should forget
lessons.why: Long tasks fail when agents lose track of what they already did. Both providers now treat context as a resource to manage deliberately. Good memory design is what separates a demo from an agent that works for hours.
openai: Building reliable agents with memory and compaction
An evidence-review agent that manages long context
anthropic: Effective context engineering for AI agents
Manage limited attention across long tasks
Store and read information across conversations
try: Give an agent a 20-step task, such as reviewing 20 short documents.
Run it once with no memory strategy and once with a notes file it updates after each step.
Compare where each run lost track or repeated work.
check: What is compaction, and what can it lose?
What belongs in long-term memory versus the current context?
How could stale memory cause a wrong answer?

lessons.title: Model Context Protocol and Integrations
lessons.summary: Connect AI to your tools and data through the open MCP standard
goals: Explain MCP servers, clients, tools and resources
Build a small MCP server
Bring an MCP server into ChatGPT and into Claude
lessons.why: MCP is the shared standard both providers support for connecting models to outside systems. Build an integration once and it works across many AI products. That makes it one of the highest-leverage skills in this course.
openai: Apps that run inside ChatGPT, built on MCP
Build to the open MCP Apps standard first
anthropic: Build MCP servers and clients in Python
Call tools through code to save context
try: Build an MCP server with one tool that reads a CSV of your choice.
Connect it to Claude and to ChatGPT.
Ask the same question in both and note any differences in how the tool was used.
check: What problem does MCP solve that plain function calling does not?
What should you check before connecting a third-party MCP server?
Which internal system would you expose through MCP first, and why?
lessons.compare: MCP is an open standard, so a server you write once can serve both. Anthropic's courses teach you to write servers and clients. OpenAI's Apps SDK uses MCP to put your app inside ChatGPT. Write the server first, then choose the front end by where your users already work.

lessons.title: Skills and Plugins
lessons.summary: Package know-how so any agent can reuse it
goals: Write a SKILL.md with a clear description and steps
Explain how skills load only when needed
Bundle skills, tools and settings into a plugin
lessons.why: Skills capture how your team does a job, so an agent can repeat it consistently. Both Codex and Claude now use the same SKILL.md folder format. Writing good skills is a skill that non-engineers can learn too.
openai: SKILL.md folders that load only when needed
Bundle skills, MCP servers, apps and hooks
anthropic: Equipping agents for the real world with Agent Skills
How Skills work and how to write them
try: Pick one report or review you produce repeatedly.
Write a SKILL.md that describes when to use it and the exact steps.
Install it in Codex or Claude Code and run it on a fresh example.
check: Why does the skill description matter more than its length?
What belongs in a skill versus a one-off prompt?
How would you share and version skills across a team?

lessons.title: Coding Agents: Codex and Claude Code
lessons.summary: Delegate real software work and verify the results
goals: Set up Codex and Claude Code on a small project
Write project guidance in AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md
Review agent changes with tests and diffs before merging
lessons.why: Coding agents are where agentic AI is most mature today. OpenAI's harness engineering post and Anthropic's best practices both describe engineers moving from typing code to directing and checking it. Leaders should understand this shift even if they never write code.
openai: Scope tasks and verify changes · 80 min
From first prompts to autonomous workflows
A product built with Codex writing every line
anthropic: Long sessions you can steer and verify
Claude Code: best practices for agentic coding
try: Pick a small repo and write a one-page AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md.
Ask each agent to add one feature with tests.
Review both diffs and record what you had to correct.
check: What belongs in a project guidance file?
Why are tests the most important input you can give a coding agent?
What changes for an engineering manager when agents write most of the code?
lessons.compare: Codex and Claude Code cover the same job, and both run from the terminal and in an editor. Preference here depends heavily on your codebase and how your team reviews changes. Give both the same real task from your own repository, review the two results the way you would review a colleague's work, and keep the one that needed fewer corrections.

lessons.title: Computer Use and Browser Agents
lessons.summary: Agents that operate screens, browsers and apps
goals: Explain the screenshot → action loop
Choose between computer use, browser tools and an API integration
Identify prompt-injection risks in agents that read web pages
lessons.why: Many systems have no API, so agents need to use them the way people do. That power comes with new risks, because every web page an agent reads can contain instructions. This lesson pairs the capability with the defenses.
openai: Operate interfaces through screenshots and actions
Hardening ChatGPT Atlas against prompt injection
Finding and fixing attacks on browser agents
try: Run a computer use demo in a sandbox, never on your main machine.
Give it a simple form-filling task.
Add a page with a hidden instruction and see whether the agent follows it; write down the defense you would add.
check: When is computer use the wrong choice?
What is prompt injection, and why are browser agents especially exposed?
Which actions should always require a human to confirm?

lessons.title: Long-Running and Managed Agents
lessons.summary: Run agents for hours in hosted harnesses and sandboxes
goals: Compare running your own agent loop with a managed agent service
Explain what a harness does for long tasks
Plan sandboxes, permissions and costs for a hosted agent
lessons.why: In 2026 both providers launched hosted agent runtimes: OpenAI's Agents API and Anthropic's Claude Managed Agents. They remove much of the infrastructure work for long-running tasks. Knowing when to rent the harness and when to own it is now an architecture decision.
openai: Managed Codex harness with sandbox choices
Run autonomous Codex agents from a Linear board
try: Choose a task that takes a person at least an hour, such as a market scan.
Write the agent definition: instructions, tools, sandbox and stop conditions.
Estimate the cost per run and decide whether a hosted or self-run harness fits better.
check: What does a harness add on top of a model and tools?
When would compliance push you toward a self-hosted sandbox?
How would you know a long-running agent has gone off track?

lessons.title: Evaluating AI Systems
lessons.summary: Prove quality with evals before and after you ship
goals: Build a small eval set from real examples
Grade outputs with code checks, model graders and human review
Track regressions when prompts, models or tools change
lessons.why: Without evals, every change to a prompt or model is a guess. Evals turn quality into numbers that leaders can trust and engineers can improve. Both providers treat them as the foundation of production AI.
openai: Evals, failure analysis, regression prevention · 70 min
Quality, latency, reliability and cost · 30 min
try: Collect 20 real inputs for one AI feature you built in this course.
Write the expected outcome for each and a pass/fail rule.
Run the set, change one thing in the prompt, and run it again.
check: Why should eval cases come from real usage?
When is a model grader trustworthy, and when do you need a person?
What eval result would make you stop a launch?
lessons.compare: OpenAI's courses give you a step-by-step method for evals, failure analysis and regression checks, which fits a single application with defined inputs and outputs. Anthropic's article focuses on agents that work across many turns, where a single right answer is harder to define. Use the first to set up your evaluation set and the second when you start grading agents.

lessons.title: Safety, Security and Governance
lessons.summary: Guardrails, oversight and what frontier research teaches about risk
goals: Map the main risks of agents with real access
Explain each provider's framework for frontier risk
Set approval points and monitoring for an agent you run
lessons.why: As agents gain access to systems and data, mistakes and misuse get more expensive. Both providers publish their own risk frameworks and incident findings, which give you a grounded view of what can go wrong. Use them to set guardrails before something breaks.
openai: How OpenAI tracks and gates frontier risks
The Hugging Face incident and the road ahead
Models in a cyber eval got around isolation controls
Detecting misbehavior in frontier reasoning models
anthropic: Stress tests of 16 models in simulated companies
try: Take the agent you designed in Lesson 17.
List every action it can take and rate each as low, medium or high impact.
Add a human approval step for every high-impact action and a log for the rest.
check: What did the agentic misalignment and Hugging Face findings have in common?
Which actions should never be fully automated in your organization?
How would you explain your agent's safeguards to a risk committee?

lessons.title: Managing AI-Enabled Teams
lessons.summary: Redesign team workflows, set review standards and coach people as AI takes on more of the work
goals: Map a team workflow and decide which steps go to AI, which stay with people, and where review happens
Set quality standards for AI-assisted work that the whole team follows
Measure whether AI is helping and coach the team through the change
lessons.why: Most AI adoption happens one team at a time, and managers decide how it lands. A manager who redesigns the work, sets clear review standards and measures results gets far more from AI than one who only hands out tools. This lesson turns the earlier ideas into a plan for your own team.
openai: Turn tasks into repeatable workflows with review points · 75–90 min
Delegate structured tasks with checkpoints and oversight · 75–90 min
Turn one opportunity into a solution plan · 30 min
anthropic: Collaborate with AI effectively, efficiently, ethically and safely
Hand Claude multi-step work on real files
Package team know-how so agents can reuse it
try: Pick one workflow your team runs every week, such as a weekly report or a customer reply process.
Map each step and mark it AI, person, or AI with human review; write the review checklist for the reviewed steps.
Run the new version for two weeks and compare time spent and error rate with the old one.
check: Which steps in your team's work should never go to AI without review, and why?
What would a fair quality standard for AI-assisted work look like on your team?
How will you tell whether AI is helping your team, beyond how often people use it?

lessons.title: Leading AI Adoption
lessons.summary: Strategy, roadmaps and helping a whole organization use AI well
goals: Find and rank AI opportunities by value and feasibility
Draft an AI strategy with governance and an adoption plan
Measure adoption and impact after launch
lessons.why: Tools are rarely the bottleneck; people, processes and priorities are. Both academies now offer courses built for leaders. This final lesson connects everything you learned to the decisions leaders make.
openai: Turn an opportunity into a solution plan · 30 min
Scale Codex Across Governed Teams and Systems
Parallel work, governance, safe integration · 100 min
anthropic: Nonprofits, small businesses, educators, creative work
What hosted agents mean for teams
try: List ten AI opportunities in your organization.
Score each on value, feasibility and risk, using what you learned in this course.
Write a one-page plan for the top two: owner, pilot scope, success metric, review date.
check: Which of your top opportunities needs an agent, and which needs a workflow?
How will you measure adoption beyond logins?
What would make you stop or expand a pilot after 90 days?

stages.name: Get started with AI
stages.project: A reusable AI workflow for one task you do every week, with a saved prompt and a review step
stages.scenario: An executive research assistant: turn a set of reports into a one-page brief you can check against the sources
checklist: You can write a prompt that gives the same quality of result three times in a row
You have handed one multi-step task to an assistant and checked what it did
You can explain when a task needs an agent and when a single prompt is enough

stages.name: Build AI applications
stages.project: A small application that calls a model API, uses one tool and returns structured output
stages.scenario: An automated weekly report: pull figures from a data source and produce the same report format every week
checklist: Your application runs end to end from a single command
Its output follows a fixed schema every time
It answers from your own documents and shows where each answer came from

stages.name: Build agents
stages.project: A working agent that uses at least one tool integration through MCP and one reusable skill
stages.scenario: A customer support agent: look up an order, draft a reply and hand off to a person when it is unsure
checklist: Your agent completes a multi-step task without you guiding each step
It connects to at least one real tool or data source
You can explain what it remembers between steps and why

stages.name: Run advanced agents
stages.project: One real task completed by a coding or long-running agent, with a written review of what it did
stages.scenario: An AI-assisted software review: have a coding agent review a pull request and compare its findings with a human review
checklist: You have reviewed an agent's full work log, not only its final answer
You set limits on what the agent could access before it started
You can name one task you would not hand to an agent yet, and why

stages.name: Safety and governance
stages.project: An evaluation set of 20 real inputs with expected outcomes, plus a one-page risk checklist for one AI use case
stages.scenario: Before launch of an internal AI assistant: test it on real questions and decide what needs human approval
checklist: You can rerun your evaluation after any prompt or model change
You have written down who approves what the AI is allowed to do
You know which failures would stop a launch

stages.name: Lead and manage
stages.project: A tested team workflow with before-and-after measures, and a prioritized AI adoption plan
stages.scenario: A team's recurring workflow: decide which steps AI handles, who reviews them, and compare time and error rates over two weeks
checklist: One team workflow has run with AI for two weeks with a named reviewer
You measured time and error rates before and after
Your adoption plan ranks use cases by value and risk
